What happens to my Apple iCloud when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 15 Oct 2026

Short answer: With a Legacy Contact, that person uses their access key and your death certificate to request your iCloud data, such as photos, messages, notes, files and backups. Without one, Apple requires legal documentation, often a court order; Apple says Australia and some other countries accept alternative documents. Keychain passwords and purchased media are never included.

Key facts

  • Legacy Contact needs: access key + death certificate
  • Excluded: iCloud Keychain and purchased media
  • No Legacy Contact: court order or local equivalent
  • Australia: Apple accepts alternative documentation

How do I prepare my Apple iCloud account?

  1. On iPhone go to Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security → Legacy Contact.
  2. Tap Add Legacy Contact, choose one or more people, and share the access key (it can also be printed).
  3. Store the printed key with your will.
  4. For a loved one who has died: request access at digital-legacy.apple.com with the access key and death certificate.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • Legacy Contact route: the access key and a death certificate
  • Without a Legacy Contact: death certificate plus a court order or the documentation Apple accepts in your country
  • To delete the account: your own Apple Account and the required legal documents

How long does it take?

Apple reviews and verifies documentation before acting and doesn't publish a fixed processing time.

What can't be recovered?

  • iCloud Keychain passwords, passkeys and payment info
  • Purchased movies, music, books and subscriptions
  • Some end-to-end encrypted data may need a device passcode
  • A passcode-locked device can't be unlocked by Apple without erasing it

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my Apple iCloud when I die?

With a Legacy Contact, that person uses their access key and your death certificate to request your iCloud data, such as photos, messages, notes, files and backups. Without one, Apple requires legal documentation, often a court order; Apple says Australia and some other countries accept alternative documents. Keychain passwords and purchased media are never included.

Does a Legacy Contact get my passwords?

No. Keychain passwords are excluded, so pair it with a password manager that has emergency access.

What if no Legacy Contact was set?

Apple generally requires a court order for family to get the data.

Can Apple unlock a dead person's iPhone?

No. Apple says it can't remove a device passcode without erasing the device. It may help remove Activation Lock so the device can be reused.

Is a court order needed in Australia?

Apple says Australia and some other jurisdictions accept alternative documentation instead of a court order; check Apple's page for your country.
